correctness.rationale: For ordinary irreducible traces under probability Haar, Schur orthogonality gives exactly |a|²+|b|² for the squared L² norm. The primitive exterior square has weights (±1,±1) and one zero weight after removing the invariant line. The four positive C₂ roots give kernel constant term 8; independent exact integer Laurent convolution yielded rows (3,0,2,0,3), (14,0,11,0,10,0,15), and (84,0,75,0,73,0,75,0,105) in degrees 4, 6, 8. Central parity kills odd indices; every retained mixed term in F^m times its conjugate has a positive moment. In interior magnitudes the (i,j)=(0,2) term and its conjugate force relative phase 0 or π at equality, and this suffices for all terms. Binomial expansion gives H₆=15+105p−90p²−16p³ and H₈=105+1680p−560p²−2240p³+1099p⁴. The first derivative H₆′ decreases strictly and is positive at 1/2; H₈′/28 decreases strictly by h′≤−9p−40 and has h(1/2)=−3/8. Both derivatives change sign from positive at 0 to negative at 1, proving unique interior maximizers and the strict change of dominant mass. The degree-four row gives 3+6p(1−p). Independent evaluation gives K₆≈43.019700544257631 and K₈≈593.699634602355104; the last printed digits in the source are approximate, and the exact definitions H₆(p₆), H₈(p₈) are confirmed.
residual_risks: No claim of expert or formal verification; phase rigidity concerns relative phase only, with arbitrary common complex scalar.

value.rationale: The span is the natural packet of the first two centered fundamental characteristic-polynomial coefficients. At fixed coefficient energy the optimal allocation is balanced at order four, favors one coefficient at six, and favors the other at eight. This gives an exact test of exponent-dependent extremizers and classifies all complex optimizers. The signs depend on mixed moments and are not a consequence of positivity, representation dimension, or the existence of a moment table.
residual_risks: The result is fixed-rank and fixed-support, not an all-exponent phase diagram or a new genus-two moment-calculus theorem.
